catalog_quote: [8.10, p.216] inherited length is never found on the ultima, and in most Bs dialects (except Mas, Sor, N-S, S-L, War) is restricted to the penult. All Bs speech varieties except some dialects of Kuy and Tsg retain phonemic accent. The following minimal pair is found in all dialects and establishes contrastive accent for PBS: punuq [pU:nuq] tree trunk < PBS *punuq and punuq [punuq] full < PBS *punuq. ... [8.10.2, p.218] In all Bs dialects studied, a closed penult is stressed. Thus, stress is predictable from the shape of the form ... Regardless of the accent on the base form, if morphophonemic changes produce a form with a CVC-penult, the penult is stressed. ... [3.1.3, pp.50-51] The accentual systems of all other Bs dialects have phonetic details involving both vowel length and stress. The vowel in an accented open penult (CV) is long: all dialects (but Kuy and Tsg) bataq → ba:taq young…

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every segment of the deciding quotation is present in the held Zorc 1977 PDF at the stated pdf pages 240, 242 and 74-75 (letter-spaced scanned, accents lost, substance verbatim); Bty = Bantayan I. confirmed in Zorc's sigla. (2) Deciding source is a 1977 comparative dialect survey whose accent statements are explicitly pan-Bisayan ('all Bs dialects studied', exceptions named and Bty not among them); Glottolog lists nothing else descriptive for bant1293. (3) Search located and fetched sources the one Bantayanon-specific description, Allen 2022 (Tulane PhD, open, 198 pp): p.90 'stress is contrastive' with minimal pair ánay 'termite' / anáy 'sow', p.143 hábuy 'blanket' / habúy 'dull', and pp.90-91 non-neutral suffixes -an/-un move stress rightward to the new penult — this independently confirms LEXICAL (contrastive penult/ultima accent with morphological conditioning) for this exact lan

sources.quote: p.90: 'In addition to the phonemes of the language, stress is contrastive. (16) ánay noun termite (17) anáy noun sow (pig); adverb for a brief moment.' pp.90-91: 'These suffixes [-un, -an] are also non-neutral; when affixed, stress is moved rightward and maintained in the penultimate (previously final) syllable. sources.note: Only Bantayanon-specific grammatical description in existence; our record rested solely on Zorc's pan-Bisayan 1977 survey statements. fetched sources now: confirms contrastive stress with Bty minimal pairs (ánay/anáy, hábuy/habúy) and suffix-induced rightward stress shift; should be added as a second citation.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Mānoa. ScholarSpace hdl 10125/101972.
sources.quote: No Bantayanon stress rule stated; Bantayanon forms are cited with lexical accent marks (Table 4.14: 'ka nákon', 'kamó nákon'); general remark p.287 fn.3 that some Philippine subgroup members have lost contrastive stress while others retain it (Bikol, Cordilleran; most Mindanao languages lost it) — Bantayanon not named among losers.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2009. Change Request 2009-082 (J. Lobel & W. Hall): create [bfx] Bantayanon, split from Hiligaynon [hil]; adopted 2010-01-18.
